status: pre-design. The entry corpus/knowledge/storage-health-r26.json, the tool tools/check-storage-health.py, the round-26 lesson corpus/lessons/round-26.md and the committed source snapshots do not exist yet. Every op is declared against the file names and the JSON shape fixed by the round-26 declaration (SCORECARD.md:895-897), so the catalogue applies unchanged once the L1 lands them.

rule_source.note: The C1 row rule is one sentence-long paragraph at SCORECARD.md:897. Each mutant below names the clause it attacks.

detector.kill_rule: A mutant is killed when the detector does not report verified_rows == 6 with exit 0. It survived when the detector still reports (6, 0). A mutant whose edit cannot be applied, or whose detector run crashed, is inconclusive, never killed.
detector.baseline_rule: The pristine sandbox must first report (6, 0). If the baseline is not (6, 0) every mutant verdict is inconclusive, because a failing baseline cannot kill a mutant.
detector.finding_ids: The predicted finding ids below follow the round-25 convention (tools/check-memory-pressure.py:844-905, ids like MP-SOURCE-STATUS-NOT-MINED). They are predictions, marked finding_is_prediction; the runner records the actual ids the detector prints.
detector.note: The detector does not exist yet. The runner reads its --help to learn whether it accepts --repo; if it does not, the runner runs the sandbox copy of the tool with the working directory set to the sandbox.

entry_shape.note: The task fixes rows[].id, verdict, action, sources, quotes[].text and capture_pointers[].line/token. The runner resolves the quote text key as text, then quote, and the quote source key as source, then source_id, so the catalogue survives the round-25 naming (quote) as well as the declared naming (text).
entry_shape.json_serialisation: JSON mutants re-serialise the entry with indent=1 and a trailing newline, keeping key order. The whole-file diff is therefore larger than the semantic delta; the semantic delta is the one named in the mutant.

capture_facts.note: Line numbers are 1-based into the frozen capture at sha256 002bef16de9bfbffff7905904a1e7f44dae486ca2e60f38090ac2a87132a71dd. The runner locates the non-unique line by text, not by number, so the locator survives a re-frozen capture.

op_vocabulary.json_row_duplicate: append a second copy of the row object with the given id
op_vocabulary.json_row_delete: delete the row with the given id
op_vocabulary.json_row_clone_with_id: append a copy of row `from` with its id replaced by `id`
op_vocabulary.json_row_set: set one field of the row with the given id to `value`
op_vocabulary.json_row_text_append: append `suffix` to the text field of the row
op_vocabulary.json_quote_set: set the quote text of the row's quotes to `text`
op_vocabulary.json_quote_lengthen: pad the quote text with filler words to exactly `words` words
op_vocabulary.json_quote_mangle: mutation `collapse_first_space`: replace the first space with an underscore, else append `x`
op_vocabulary.json_quote_source_set: set the quote source id of the row quotes to `value`
op_vocabulary.json_capture_pointers_set: replace every capture pointer of the row with one {line, token}
op_vocabulary.json_capture_pointers_token_set: replace every capture pointer token of the row with `value`
op_vocabulary.json_capture_pointers_empty: empty the capture pointer list of the row
op_vocabulary.sources_row_set: set one cell of the corpus/SOURCES.md registry row of the target source ids
op_vocabulary.gate_quote_mangle: mutate the quoted text inside the lesson Gate table row of the target source id
op_vocabulary.gate_row_delete: delete the lesson Gate table row of the target source id
op_vocabulary.snapshot_byte_change: append a trailing space to the committed snapshot of the target source id
op_vocabulary.skill_first_cell_set: set the first cell of the row's table line inside the SKILL.md section to `value`
op_vocabulary.skill_row_delete: delete the row's table line inside the SKILL.md section
op_vocabulary.skill_row_move_out: move the row's table line to the end of SKILL.md, outside the section
op_vocabulary.capture_append_line: append one line to the frozen capture
op_vocabulary.json_row_add_source: append one source id to the row sources list

mutants.notes: The clone is a fully valid row with a seventh id. verified_rows 0 is the round-25 convention for a wrong row id set (a global block sets the count to 0); a per-row reading gives 6 with exit 1. Either way the exit must not be 0.

mutants.rule: R1 ids: exactly SH1 to SH6 (id spelling)

mutants.rule: R2 fields: the row has a verdict from HEALTHY, DEGRADED, BLOCKED, UNVERIFIED
mutants.clause: SCORECARD.md:897 - 'a verdict (HEALTHY, DEGRADED, BLOCKED or UNVERIFIED)'
mutants.notes: A free-text verdict must not count as one of the four.

mutants.rule: R2 fields: the row has a verdict
mutants.notes: An empty verdict is not a verdict. A tool that defaults a missing verdict to a constant survives here.

mutants.rule: R2 fields: the row has a non-empty statement
mutants.clause: SCORECARD.md:897 - 'the row has a non-empty statement'
mutants.notes: An empty statement carries no claim and must not count.

mutants.rule: R2 fields: the row has an action
mutants.notes: An empty action is not an action.

mutants.rule: R2 fields: the verdict vocabulary is the four upper-case states
mutants.notes: Case-folded acceptance is a reading of the rule, not the rule. A tool that lower-cases before comparing survives this mutant; that survivor is a wording question for the L1, not a silent hole.

expectation.notes_extra: The mutated sources may also be cited by another row, in which case that row fails too and the count falls further.

expectation.notes_extra: The mutated sources may also be cited by another row, in which case that row fails too and the count falls further.

mutants.rule: R3 sources: every cited source names corpus/knowledge/storage-health-r26.md in used-by
mutants.notes: The used-by cell names another entry, so the source is not credited to this entry. A tool that accepts any corpus/knowledge path survives.

mutants.notes: Every tier A source of the whole entry is demoted to B. Each row then fails the tier clause, so the count must fall to 0.

mutants.rule: R4 quote: at least one quote of at most 25 words
mutants.clause: SCORECARD.md:897 - 'at least one quote of at most 25 words'
mutants.notes: Every quote of the row is padded to 26 words, so no short quote survives. If the row carries a second, shorter quote that the padding skips, the row may still count: the runner pads all quotes and the catalogue records the word counts it found.

mutants.rule: R4 quote: the snapshot's sha256 is written in the source's anchor cell

mutants.rule: R4 quote: the same quote text appears in that source's row of the lesson Gate table

mutants.notes: The entry quote is untouched; only the lesson Gate cell changes, so the two no longer agree. A tool that reports the mismatch as a finding but still counts the row survives - that is exactly the 'never only a finding' clause.

mutants.rule: R4 quote: the same quote text appears in that source's row of the lesson Gate table

mutants.notes: A two-character token is too short even when the line contains it.
